text:
Harlow & Voss LLP – Privacy Notice for Clients

We collect personal data only to the extent that it is necessary for the provision of our legal services and for compliance with our professional obligations. [1] Data supplied in the course of an engagement is stored on servers located within the European Economic Area and is retained for a period of seven years after the matter has closed.

We do not disclose personal data to third parties, [2] where disclosure is required by law or has been authorized by the client in writing. Clients are entitled to request access to the data we hold about them, and to ask that inaccurate information be [3]. Requests of this kind will be answered within thirty days, [4] that period may be extended where a request is particularly complex.

choices: The firm does not use such data for marketing purposes and does not share it with any affiliated business.
The firm uses such data for marketing purposes and shares it only with affiliated businesses that hold a license.
The firm does not use such data for archiving purposes and does not store it in any affiliated business.
The firm did not use such data for marketing purposes, but now shares it with every affiliated business.
questions.explanation: The notice says data is collected 'only to the extent ... necessary' and, in the next paragraph, not disclosed to third parties; only the first option is consistent with both. The others admit marketing or sharing, discuss archiving, or use a tense that contradicts the present policy.

'Except where disclosure is required by law' introduces the exception to the rule; 'unless' would need a clause with a verb in the same position ('unless disclosure is required'), and 'whereas' and 'although' do not state exceptions.
After 'be', the passive requires the past participle 'rectified' (corrected).
'Although that period may be extended' concedes an exception to the thirty-day promise; the others do not fit the logic.

text:
CITY OF EASTMOOR – NOTICE OF TEMPORARY ROAD CLOSURE

In order to allow the replacement of a main sewer, Quay Street will be closed to all traffic between its junctions with Mill Lane and Orchard Road from 6 a.m. on Monday 14 April until 6 p.m. on Friday 25 April. [1] Access for pedestrians will be maintained at all times, and businesses within the closed section will remain open.

Diversion routes will be signposted. Motorists [2] to reach the town center from the north are advised to use the ring road, which is expected to carry [3] more traffic than usual. Deliveries to affected premises may be made through the rear service lane, [4] vehicles exceeding 7.5 tonnes will not be permitted to use it.

choices: Emergency vehicles will be able to pass through the works area, but only at reduced speed and under supervision.
Emergency vehicles will be unable to pass through the works area, and no access will be provided under any supervision.
Heavy vehicles will be able to pass through the works area, but only at reduced speed and under supervision.
Emergency vehicles were able to pass through the works area, but only at reduced speed and without supervision.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says 'Access for pedestrians will be maintained', so the previous one should address another category of access; the first option allows emergency vehicles. The others contradict the closure for 'all traffic', admit heavy vehicles, or use a past tense.
'Motorists wishing to reach' uses a present participle as a reduced relative clause ('who wish'); the other forms are ungrammatical here.
'Considerably more traffic' is the adverb modifying the comparative 'more'; the other forms are not adverbs.
'Although vehicles exceeding 7.5 tonnes will not be permitted' concedes a limit to the permission; 'provided' needs 'that', and 'because' and 'unless' invert the logic.

text:
Subject: Draft proposal for the Aldgate redevelopment

Dear Mr. Whitlow,

Please find attached our draft proposal for the redevelopment of the Aldgate site. We have prepared it in the light of your comments at last week's meeting, and we have [1] a number of the concerns that you raised regarding access and parking.

[2] The proposal assumes that the existing warehouse can be retained, which would reduce demolition costs by roughly a fifth. This assumption has yet to be confirmed by the structural engineer, [3] the figures should be treated as provisional. I should be grateful if you would let me have your comments by Friday, [4] we can incorporate them in the version that goes to the planning committee.

questions.explanation: One 'addresses' concerns by dealing with them; 'adjourned' means postponed, 'adjusted' means modified, and 'admitted' means confessed.

choices: The most significant change concerns the schedule, which now reflects a more cautious estimate of the benefit of the project.
The most significant change concerns the budget, which now reflects a more cautious estimate of the cost of the project.
The most significant change concerns the access road, which now reflects a more cautious estimate of the cost of the project.
The least significant change concerns the budget, which now reflects a more cautious estimate of the cost of the project.
questions.explanation: The next sentence discusses the cost saving from retaining the warehouse, so the previous one should introduce the budget; only the first does. The others turn to the schedule, the access road, or the least significant change, none of which leads to cost figures.
'And so the figures should be treated as provisional' states the consequence of the unconfirmed assumption; the other options express contrast.
'So that we can incorporate them' states the purpose of the deadline; 'in order' lacks 'that', 'provided' needs 'that', and 'lest' requires a negative idea.

text:
The Wexford Institute of Management – Executive Diploma in Strategy

Designed for senior professionals who wish to broaden their strategic perspective, the Executive Diploma in Strategy is delivered over nine months in a flexible format that [1] full-time employment. Teaching is shared between academics and practitioners who currently hold senior positions in industry.

[2] Participants work in small groups on live commercial problems submitted by partner companies, and the results are presented to the companies' directors at the end of the program. [3] the course is demanding, graduates consistently report that it was the most valuable investment of their careers. Applications received [4] 30 June will be considered for a bursary covering up to a third of the fee.

questions.explanation: A format that 'accommodates' full-time employment makes room for it; 'accumulates', 'accomplishes' and 'acknowledges' do not take that object sensibly.

choices: The curriculum places particular emphasis on studying theory in the abstract rather than on applying it to real situations.
The curriculum places particular emphasis on applying theory to real situations rather than on studying it in the abstract.
The curriculum places particular emphasis on applying theory to real situations rather than on teaching it to practitioners.
The previous curriculum placed particular emphasis on applying theory to real situations rather than on studying it.
questions.explanation: The next sentence describes work on live commercial problems, which is the application of theory; only the first sentence prepares it. The others invert the emphasis, add an irrelevant contrast, or describe a previous curriculum.
'Although the course is demanding' concedes a drawback before the positive claim; the others do not express concession.
'Applications received before 30 June' gives the deadline for the bursary; 'during' and 'within' do not fit a fixed date and 'since' needs a past reference.
